title: Generalized p-Brauer supercharacters of cyclic Tate cohomology are explicit trace combinations for finite free p-adic lattices with central composite-order action
author: Satoru Urano
work: A Composite Order Generalization of Modular Moonshine
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 110, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.110; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof handles finite-length modules over ramified valuation rings rather than ordinary modular vector spaces. It proves ramification-invariance of the normalized Brauer character, computes cyclic Tate cohomology lengths for eigenlattices, and uses inverse finite Fourier transforms and cyclotomic sums to obtain the exact trace coefficients. These length and ramification obligations go beyond the prime-order Brauer character formula.

The selected base ring is Z_p, with the author's finite cyclotomic extension used in the proof; no broader ambiguity about simultaneous mixed residue characteristics is imported. The primitive-root valuation formula is identified prior background. Theorem4.4 moonshine vanishing has a proof referred back to an earlier paper and is not selected, nor is the computational Monster counterexample. Native source confirms the complex conjugation bar in the Fourier transform, lost by text extraction. retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem5.7 restricted to R=Z_p for a fixed prime p dividing N: finite group G, central g of order N, h N-regular, A finite free Z_p-module with the commuting g,h action. The virtual cyclic Tate module Hhat0(g,A)-Hhat1(g,A) has the normalized p-Brauer character of Definition5.1, equal to the displayed sum over 1<=k<N with precisely the author coefficients a_k,p. The integral-lattice restriction and finite cyclotomic base change are explicit; no unqualified ordinary Brauer-vector-space or Monster vanishing claim is added.
